newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso urges quick vote on re-election.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso urges quick vote on re-election.

text.p: Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Tuesday urged opponents to stop delaying voting on a bill that would allow him to stand for re-election.

"Congress must assume its responsibilties and feel, along with everybody else, that now is the time. The whole country knows this issue has to be decided," Cardoso said shortly after Congress postponed a first vote on re-election.

The president, speaking to members of his Brazilian Social Democratic Party (PSDB) said reforms considered crucial to the long-term stability of Brazil's economy were being delayed by the re-election debate.
"We cannot postpone social security, tax and civil service reform just to discuss whether so-and-so and such-and-such is going to be benefited by a decision," he said.

Cardoso wants to become Brazil's first re-elected president since the founding of the republic in 1889, saying that support for his inflation-slashing economic policies entitled him the right to stand for a second term.
A first panel-level vote on a re-election bill was delayed on Tuesday as Congress' most powerful party, the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), remained divided on the issue.

Later, however, the PMDB's six members of the panel said they would vote in favour of re-election at a rescheduled session on Wednesday. "They will vote and they will vote in favour," a PMDB spokesman said.

Analysts said the outcome of the struggle between the pro- and anti-government wings of the PMDB would determine not only whether Cardoso would be allowed to run again in 1998, but also the prospects of other reforms to streamline the state during the remainder of his first term.
"The government has made re-election such a priority that its entire reform programme is practically dependent on it," political analyst Ricardo Pedreira said.
